sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by anti-myc immunofluorescence on fixed HEK-293 cells; receptor function not explicitly assayed in the cited experiment.
sites.rationale: GPRC6A is a class-C GPCR with a large extracellular N-terminal domain (residues 19–593) and an intracellular C-terminus (residues 832–926). The signal peptide spans residues 1–18 (last SP residue = S18, first mature residue = Q19), so a tag upstream of Q19 would be cleaved. Because the C-terminus is cytoplasmic, the mature N-terminus is the only extracellular face available for a surface-detectable tag, making insert_after_residue=18 the topology-derived junction. Python confirmed S at position 18 and Q at position 19 from the canonical sequence. Mouse GPRC6A stably expressed in HEK-293 cells with a myc tag; anti-myc antibody staining of paraformaldehyde-fixed cells confirmed surface display of the full-length receptor. No residue number is stated in the paper. The C-terminus of GPRC6A is intracellular (residues 832–926 per landmarks), leaving the mature N-terminus (after SP cleavage at residue 18, first mature residue Q19) as the sole extracellular terminus and therefore the only position consistent with surface anti-myc staining.

sources.claim: HEK-293 cells stably transfected with a myc-tagged version of wild type mouse GPRC6A or the mutant in which KY was substituted for RKLP sequence in the 3rd intracellular loop were fixed by incubating the cells in 4% paraformaldehyde in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) for 10 min at room temperature.
For transient transfection, HEK293 cells were transfected with V5-tagged IGF1R, GFP-IR or Flag-GPRC6A plasmids with Lipofectamine 2000.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) concern N-terminal tags on full-length GPRC6A. L1 and L2 are from the same paper (PMC5490090) and describe the same myc-tagged construct; L1 is cited as the primary clip because it names both the construct and the staining method. L3 (PMC8421392) independently reports a Flag-tagged construct. No ledger line names a specific residue number, so both sites are topology_derived. The RKLP motif mentioned in L1 as the 3rd intracellular loop mutation site is recorded in other_positions. No ledger evidence supports any internal extracellular loop tag (ECL1 652–662, ECL2 726–748, ECL3 804–811) or a C-terminal extracellular tag.

literature_other_positions.note: L1 describes a mutant in which 'KY was substituted for RKLP sequence in the 3rd intracellular loop' of mouse GPRC6A; the 3rd intracellular loop (IC3) maps to residues 772–782 in the human canonical sequence, making this an intracellular position unsuitable for a surface tag.
